summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Panjab University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Cambridge. Her career includes posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1995–2006) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2013–2014).

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Hiram W. Woodward studied at Harvard College (~1958–1962) and Yale University (~1969–1975). He held posts at the University of Michigan (~1972–1982), the University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and the Walters Art Museum (~1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College, Oriental College, and Panjab University. He held positions at the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, and Baroda State Department of Archaeology (1934–1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied in the doctoral course at Taisho University (attested 2013) and subsequently held a post there as a research student (研究生).

Hirofumi Isoda is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1961–1966). He served at Tohoku University as lecturer (attested 1972) and associate professor (~1977–2001), and as professor emeritus at Shimane University (attested 1974).

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1980–2001) and as a special researcher at Rissho University (attested 1985).
Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist and religious studies and studied under John Okell and Anna Allott. She held a post as senior lecturer at Lancaster University, attested from 2013 to 2016.
Hiroko Matsuoka is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and later held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

Hiromasa Tosaki works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and Harvard University under scholars including Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Satkari Mookerjee, and Shoren Ihara. He served as professor at Kyushu University (~1978–1994).
Hiromi Habata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg. She held a research post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2014).
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who held posts at Ryukoku University, including as full-time lecturer (専任講師) attested in 1987 and later attested in 2006.
Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor (~1971–1990).
Hironori Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and later held a post there.

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Matsusaka University (attested 1982) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College.
Hiroshi Aoyagi is a scholar of Japanology. He studied at International Christian University and held a post at Nanzan University around 2008.

Hiroshi Araki specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from Kyoto University. He held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1989–1994), Osaka University (~1994–2010), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2010 onwards as professor).

Hiroshi Kanno is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1982). He served as director at Soka University (~1992–2022) and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~1999–2009).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. His academic career includes holding an associate professorship at the University of Tokyo between 1992 and 2018.
Hiroshi Maruyama is a scholar of Indology who served as a professor at Osaka University and led the Ayurveda Kenkyūkai, both attested in 1987.
Hiroshi Nemoto specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned an MA from Hiroshima University and later served there as a professor, attested in 2015.
